newsitem.title: DENMARK: A.P. Moeller pushes Danish shares to record high.
newsitem.headline: A.P. Moeller pushes Danish shares to record high.

text.p: Danish share prices closed on a record high on Friday, for the fourth consecutive day. Dealers said that sentiment was positive but further developments would depend on trade in New York on Friday afternoon and on Monday, when Danish markets are closed for the Whit holiday.
"It has again been a day of record rising prices and the underlying trend remains positive but it is difficult to say what will happen on Tuesday," a dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed 2.07 point up -- a 1.25 percent rise -- to stand at 167.92 and its June future was up 2.10 point to 167.10. Total bourse turnover was 1.39 billion crowns.
Shipping group A.P.Moeller's D/S 1912 rose 8,500 crowns to 242,500 and sister D/S Svendborg was up 16,667 crowns, to 346,000, with institutional investors showing keen interest in both, dealers said.
Sophus Berendsen, part-owner of Britain's Rentokil, rose 17 crowns to 890.00 on Rentokil's split of each 2p ordinary share into two of 1p.
Den Danske Bank rose eight crowns to 628 crowns, while Unidanmark and BG Bank rose a crown each, to 354.00 and 315.00 respectively. REUTER
